relations.evidence: The `OnDeploy` handler runs once when an Eventing function is deployed or resumed, before any mutations are processed.

relations.subject: eventing:function

relations.subject: eventing:function

relations.evidence: To set the `bucket.scope` to `+`.`+`, you must have the `Eventing Full Admin` or the `Full Admin` role. All other users must use a scope that references an existing resource of their `bucket.scope`.

relations.subject: eventing:function-scope
relations.evidence: To set the `bucket.scope` to `+`.`+`, you must have the `Eventing Full Admin` or the `Full Admin` role.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: The Feed Boundary determines if the Eventing Function's activities need to include documents that already exist. When you set the Feed Boundary to Everything, the Function processes all mutations available in your cluster. When you set the Feed Boundary to From Now, the Function only processes instances of data mutation that happen after the Function's deployment.

relations.subject: eventing:function-lifecycle-state
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (usesEnum) - the Feed Boundary also functions as a resume checkpoint, coupling it to the lifecycle enum specifically
relations.evidence: The Feed Boundary also works as a checkpoint for paused Functions. When you resume a paused Function, the Feed Boundary makes sure that no mutations are lost or processed again.

relations.subject: capella:collection
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - camelCase verb phrase for a resource-deletion event forcing a dependent Function's lifecycle state to change; a lifecycle-cascade shape not previously in the registry
relations.evidence: When you delete a source collection, all deployed and paused Functions associated with the collection are undeployed.

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-storage
relations.evidence: If you delete the metadata collection, all deployed Eventing Functions are undeployed and all associated indexes and constructs are dropped.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (shouldNotBeConfusedWith) - the page explicitly warns about the distinct hazard rather than merely defining it
relations.evidence: A potentially recursive mutation happens when a handler manipulates documents in a keyspace that also serves as the mutation source for this or another handler. The write originated by the handler causes a mutation to be seen by itself or by another handler.

relations.subject: eventing:function

relations.evidence: The Function's JavaScript code can also trigger mutations on documents through inline SQL++ statements in the Query Service or `N1QL()` function calls.
